stories.title: Does GTA VI live up to the hype? Our games editor has played it – ask her anything
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI, the biggest games release of the decade, is nearly here.

Our games editor Keza MacDonald will be online from 4pm GMT (11am EST, 3am AEDT) to answer all your questionsAsk a question: log in or sign up hereAfter more than a decade and a reported billion dollars in the making, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally released on Thursday.

It’s one of the most anticipated games of all time.The Guardian’s games editor, Keza MacDonald, is one of the first people in the world to have played it and she’s now spent over 70 hours in Leonida to review the game.

stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story
summary: There is such a multiplicity of things on offer here that it is difficult to nail down what this game definitively is.
It will be different for everyone – that is the beauty of it.For me, though, this game is about Jason and Lucia, the fugitive couple through whom you experience all that Leonida has to offer.

When Lucia gets out of prison, the two of them try to make some kind of life for themselves – but before long they get caught up with the wrong people and have to flee the cosy life they’ve just started building.

stories.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year
summary: Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionaryIn a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human.Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.

stories.title: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
summary: Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spyNvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday.

Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago.

The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees.
